sentences.text: Zalmoxes was a small, bipedal herbivore characterized by a large triangular head and a beak.
This extinct genus includes two known species of ornithopod dinosaurs belonging to the subfamily Rhabdodontinae.
Subadult Zalmoxes robustus measured between 2 and 2.4 meters in total body length, while adults reached up to 2.5 meters and 45 kilograms in body mass.
The species Z. shqiperorum is the larger of the two, known from a subadult individual measuring 2.5 meters in length.
An unnamed species of Zalmoxes is known from adults reaching 2.9 meters in length.
Zalmoxes was a more robust animal than its precursors and advanced relatives, possessing a very strong morphology.
The genus name honors the Dacian deity Zalmoxis, while the species name refers to the robustness of the fossil remains.
Ossified tendons were found in the juvenile specimen of Z. shqiperorum, showing they were circular or elliptical in cross-section with fine striations.
The genus was first named in 1899 by Franz Nopcsa as the species Mochlodon robustum.
The species was reclassified as Zalmoxes robustus in 2003 after a new species was identified that year based on new remains found in Romania by Weishampel et al.
A second species, Zalmoxes shqiperorum, was named in 2003, derived from the Albanian name for Albanians.
Numerous fossils found in Transylvania were first named in 1899 by Baron Franz Nopcsa.
A 2003 study suggested Zalmoxes ate tough fibrous plants including soft shoots, horsetails, angiosperms, pteridophytes, and ferns.
Further studies indicated Zalmoxes could process and digest C3 plants.
A 2003 scientific article found that Zalmoxes likely had a diet consisting of hard fibrous plants such as soft shoots, horsetails, angiosperms, pteridophytes, and ferns.
Nopcsa proposed that Zalmoxes adapted through insular dwarfism because it was smaller than its relatives in the Hateg Basin.
While Nopcsa hypothesized that the small size of Zalmoxes was due to insular dwarfism, later research by Osi and colleagues found the size similar to that of rhabdodontid ancestors.
Nopcsa proposed that animals in the Hațeg basin, which were smaller than relatives from other areas, suffered from insular dwarfism.
In 2003, Weishampel et al. established the family Rhabdodontidae for Mochlodon, Rhabdodon, and Zalmoxes.
The family Rhabdodontidae is classified as a derived group within Iguanodontia.
Further studies have supported the classification of Rhabdodontidae, placing them phylogenetically between Talenkauen and Tenontosaurus.
The parent group for Zalmoxes is Rhabdodontoidea.
Zalmoxes belongs to the class Ornithischia.
Zalmoxes lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) in what is now Romania.
Zalmoxes lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now Europe.
The time range for Zalmoxes spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
Zalmoxes fossils are found in the Sânpetru, Sebes, and Densuş-Ciula Formations in the Hateg Island region of Romania.
Fossils of both Zalmoxes species have been unearthed in the Sânpetru, Sebes, and Densuş-Ciula Formations in Romania, found exclusively in the Hateg island region.
It is debated whether Zalmoxes shqiperorum is an ornithopod or a ceratopsian, with recent studies in 2026 placing it in Ceratopsia.
